prov.text: For the three months ended September 30, 2026, the provision for credit losses on loans was $13.1 million, which was an increase of $6.8 million from the provision recorded in the prior quarter. Compared to the same period in the prior year, the provision for credit losses on loans for the three months ended September 30, 2026 decreased $7.7 million. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the provision for credit losses on loans was $30.7 million, which was a $13.1 million decrease from the $43.8 million provision recorded in the same period last year. Changes in the provision are driven by changes in the estimate for the allowance for credit losses on loans.

nonint.heading: Non-Interest Expense
nonint.text: Non-interest expense for the third quarter of 2026 amounted to $285.9 million, an increase of $41.9 million, or 17.2%, compared to expense of $244.0 million in the third quarter of last year. The increase in expense over the same period last year was mainly due to higher salaries and employee benefits expense, data processing and software expense, professional and other services expense and intangible amortization expense. Salaries and employee benefits expense increased $24.1 million, or 15.3%, mainly due to the onboarding of FineMark's team members at the beginning of 2026. Acquisition-related salaries and benefits expense was $3.3 million in the current quarter. Full-time equivalent employees totaled 4,969 at September 30, 2026, compared to 4,666 at September 30, 2025. Additionally, healthcare expense increased $4.1 million over the same period in the prior year. Data processing and software expense increased $5.3 million, or 15.8%, mainly due to higher costs for service providers. Professional and other services expense, which increased $3.4 million, or 29.8%, included $1.2 million of acquisition-related legal and professional services expense in the current quarter. Net occupancy expense increased $1.6 million, or 11.8%, and equipment expense increased $286 thousand, or 5.3%, both mainly due to higher depreciation expense.

nonop.heading: Non-Interest Expense
nonop.text: Non-interest expense for the third quarter of 2026 amounted to $285.9 million, an increase of $41.9 million, or 17.2%, compared to expense of $244.0 million in the third quarter of last year. The increase in expense over the same period last year was mainly due to higher salaries and employee benefits expense, data processing and software expense, professional and other services expense and intangible amortization expense. Salaries and employee benefits expense increased $24.1 million, or 15.3%, mainly due to the onboarding of FineMark's team members at the beginning of 2026. Acquisition-related salaries and benefits expense was $3.3 million in the current quarter. Full-time equivalent employees totaled 4,969 at September 30, 2026, compared to 4,666 at September 30, 2025. Additionally, healthcare expense increased $4.1 million over the same period in the prior year. Data processing and software expense increased $5.3 million, or 15.8%, mainly due to higher costs for service providers. Professional and other services expense, which increased $3.4 million, or 29.8%, included $1.2 million of acquisition-related legal and professional services expense in the current quarter. Net occupancy expense increased $1.6 million, or 11.8%, and equipment expense increased $286 thousand, or 5.3%, both mainly due to higher depreciation expense.

pretax.text: For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, income before income taxes for the Retail Banking segment decreased $18.6 million, or 10.8%, compared to the first nine months of 2025. The decrease in income before income taxes was mainly due to an increase in non-interest expense of $12.9 million, or 5.1%, and a decline in net interest income of $10.0 million, or 2.6%. These decreases to income were partly offset by an increase in non-interest income of $2.3 million, or 3.2%, and a decline in the provision for credit losses of $1.9 million, or 6.6%. Net interest income declined due to lower loan interest income of $7.7 million and higher deposit interest expense of $5.8 million, partly offset by an increase in net allocated funding credits assigned to the Retail Banking segment's loan and deposit portfolios of $3.5 million. The increase in non-interest income was mainly due to growth in deposit account fees (mainly overdraft and return items fees) and bank card fee income (mainly credit card fees). Non-interest expense increased over the same period in the previous year mainly due to higher salaries and benefits expense, marketing expense, occupancy expense and allocated support and service costs (mainly technology, customer support and operations). These increases were slightly offset by a decline in miscellaneous losses.

tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text: Income tax expense was $44.4 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $45.8 million in the second quarter of 2026 and $41.2 million in the third quarter of 2025. The Company's effective tax rate, including the effect of non-controlling interest, was 22.3% in the third quarter of 2026, 22.3% in the second quarter of 2026, and 22.5% in the third quarter of 2025.

net.text: For the quarter ended September 30, 2026, net income attributable to Commerce Bancshares, Inc. (net income) amounted to $155.0 million, an increase of $13.5 million, or 9.5%, compared to the third quarter of the previous year. For the current quarter, the annualized return on average assets was 1.79%, the annualized return on average equity was 14.17%, and the efficiency ratio was 56.69%. Diluted earnings per common share was $1.08 per share in the current quarter, an increase of 6.9% compared to $1.01 per share in the third quarter of 2025, and decreased 1.8% compared to $1.10 per share in the previous quarter.

intro.text: Commerce Bancshares, Inc., a bank holding company as defined in the Bank Holding Company Act of 1956, as amended, was incorporated under the laws of Missouri on August 4, 1966. Through a second tier wholly-owned bank holding company, it owns all the outstanding capital stock of Commerce Bank (the “Bank”), which is headquartered in Missouri. The Bank engages in general banking business, providing a broad range of retail, mortgage banking, corporate, investment, trust, and asset management products and services to individuals, businesses, and municipalities. Commerce Bancshares, Inc. also owns, directly or through the Bank, various non-banking subsidiaries. Their activities include private equity investment, securities brokerage, underwriting, specialty lending, and leasing activities. A list of Commerce Bancshares, Inc.'s subsidiaries is included as Exhibit 21.

s.t: The net gains in the third quarter of 2026 were mainly comprised of net gains in fair value of $8.1 million recorded on private equity investments, net gains of $5.3 million on sales of private equity investments, and net gains of $3.1 million on equity securities, primarily related to gains recorded on the Company's shares of Visa, as described in Note 4, Investment Securities.

Net gains in the first nine months of 2026 were mainly comprised of net gains of $117.4 million on equity securities, mainly Visa common stock as described above, and net gains in fair value of $15.1 million recorded on private equity investments.

Under the terms of the merger agreement, each outstanding FineMark common stock share was converted into .7245 shares of the Company's common stock, and each outstanding share of FineMark's preferred stock was converted into 36.3636 shares of FineMark common stock, prior to conversion into .7245 shares of the Company's common stock.

At December 31, 2025, the Company’s Visa Class B-2 shares were carried at cost, which is $ 0 , as the Company elected the measurement alternative approach for these shares and there had not been observable price changes in orderly transactions for identical or similar investments of the same issuer for the Visa Class B-2 shares held by the Company.

Additionally, because the Company elected the measurement alternative approach for its Visa Class B-3 common stock, these shares will continue to be carried at cost ($ 0 ) unless there are observable price changes in orderly transactions for identical or similar investments of the same issuer for the Visa Class B-3 shares held by the Company.
